summary: Chatlet fanout causing multiplex queue-head lock and GPU attach latency in dedicated pool
description:
Issue summary:
Customer (ConvoHealth, dedicated pool) reports sustained p99 generation latency increases and intermittent request failures starting 2026-03-10 09:12 UTC. A spike in very short chat completions ("chatlets") from the customer's front-end produced a large number of simultaneous multiplexed streams which appear to block the queue head in the per-GPU batching layer, delaying GPU attach operations and causing p99 to jump from ~350ms to ~2.2s.

Impact:
- Increased p99 tail for text generation on dedicated pool, customer-facing slowdown impacting real-time chat product.
- Error rate (503/504) rose from 0.1% to 1.7% during peak window.
- Customer reports degraded UX during a marketing-driven burst; business impact medium-high.

Timeline / Observed behavior:
- 2026-03-10 09:12 UTC: Onset of increased small-completion traffic from ConvoHealth (customer logs show ~18k ~<50-token requests/min).
- 09:14–09:25: Grafana shows per-GPU attach latency spike and queue-length oscillation.
- 09:18: Node-level dmesg contains repeated NIC interrupt coalescing warnings and occasional nvidia-driver "GPU hung" trace snippets.
- 09:20: Autoscaler attempted to add allocation but observed attach delays >8s causing scaling backoff.

Environment / Context:
- Dedicated GPU pool: 8 x A200 per cluster, mixed driver revision (515.76 and 515.86) due to staggered host updates.
- Serving runtime version: 2.11.3. Scheduler version: 1.8.0.
- Customer traffic pattern: many short-lived connections that open streaming channels, send few tokens, and close quickly ("chatlets").

Steps to reproduce (customer-provided):
1) Replay recorded traffic sample (attached) against customer-dedicated endpoint during a quiet window.
2) Observe many concurrent streaming sessions with 10–40 token payloads and keep-alive churn.
3) Notice elevated attach latency and queue-head waits; replicate p99 increase in local dedicated staging.

Logs / Evidence:
- Grafana trace: https://grafana.redwood/r/tx/trace/C-gf3k2 (p99 attach spike).
- dmesg excerpt (host-120): "NETDEV_WARN: NIC interrupt-coalesce overflow ..." 
- /var/log/nvidia/gpu-manager.log: "[2026-03-10T09:18:23Z] Warning: GPU 2 attach timeout, retrying"
- Customer sample payload: s3://convohealth-shared/chatlet-sample-20260310.json

Initial hypothesis:
1) High fanout of short streaming connections produces head-of-queue serialization in the per-GPU multiplexer. Short-lived chatlets prevent efficient batching and leave many inflight handles tied to the queue head.
2) Heterogeneous driver versions + NIC interrupt anomaly increase host-side latency and exacerbate attach timing, triggering autoscaler backoff heuristics.
3) Noisy-tenant effect: many tiny streams from same customer created bursting resource contention on scheduler and network stack.

Immediate mitigation taken:
- Support increased per-tenant stream concurrency cap for ConvoHealth temporarily to reduce rapid connect/disconnect cycles (rollout 09:40 UTC).
- SRE enabled a temporary worker pool with pre-attached GPU warm slots for the customer's pool to reduce attach latency for short streams (09:52 UTC).

Open questions / next steps:
- Reproduce locally with mixed-driver hosts to confirm if driver heterogeneity materially increases attach latency.
- Evaluate changes to multiplexer fairness: move from strict FIFO head-lock to short-window re-ordering to allow small-stream bypass.
- Network team to investigate NIC interrupt coalescing incidents on affected hosts; consider driver/firmware patch or interrupt tuning.
- Consider customer-side guidance: batch small chatlets client-side or use ephemeral longer-lived streams.
comments: Priya Raman (Support) [2026-03-10 09:28]: Escalated to SRE / serving-runtime. Attached customer sample and Grafana trace. Requested immediate mitigation options.
SRE: Marta Kovac [2026-03-10 09:36]: Observed attach latency on host-118..122. Hypothesis: NIC interrupt storms + many short-lived streams. Spun pre-attached warm workers for ConvoHealth to buy time.
Luis Ortega (Oncall Serving) [2026-03-10 09:50]: Deployed temporary concurrency cap change and added warm-slot pool. Customer reports p99 dropped from 2.2s to ~420ms within 10m.
Customer (ConvoHealth - Eng Ops) [2026-03-10 10:05]: Noted improvement but still seeing occasional 1s spikes during peak. Provided additional request traces (s3 link).

Network Eng [2026-03-11 14:12]: Investigated NIC interrupts on host-120; driver telemetry shows increased irq_count correlating with attach delays. Filing ticket to infra for firmware update schedule.
Luis Ortega [2026-03-12 08:30]: Opening follow-up epic to address multiplexer head-lock: runtime design review requested. See PR linked for prototype: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4821
investigation_notes: Checked host-level metrics across impacted machines: host-118..host-122 show 3-4x baseline softirq/NAPI spikes coincident with customer burst windows.
Heap of per-GPU multiplexer: tasks stuck at head for >150ms while many <50-token streams queued behind. Batching efficiency dropped by ~65% for that workload.
Kernel logs show occasional GPU reset trace but no persistent GPU panic. Driver versions differ across hosts; need consistent baseline to rule out regressions.
Autoscaler logs: observed repeated attach timeout events causing exponential backoff; scaled down incorrectly due to perceived failed attempts.
Replayed customer's sample in staging with homogenous drivers and observed smaller attach latencies (~300-450ms) vs mixed-driver baseline (~700-1100ms) confirming heterogeneity amplifies the issue.
Concluded joint root cause: small-stream fanout (chatlet pattern) + host-level NIC interrupt noise + driver heterogeneity => queue-head lock and attach latency spikes.
resolution: Workarounds applied: 1) temporary warm-slot pool for ConvoHealth; 2) per-tenant burst throttle guidance shared. Longer-term fixes planned: multiplexer fairness algorithm change, host driver/firmware standardization, and autoscaler logic tweak to avoid over-reacting to transient attach delays. Draft runbook and action items created.

INFRA-87: Standardize NVIDIA driver across dedicated hosts and schedule firmware upgrade for NICs (owner: Network Eng)
SCHED-45: Adjust autoscaler backoff thresholds for attach-timeout events (owner: Scheduler team)
DOC-12: Customer guidance note for chatlet-heavy workloads recommending client-side batching or persistent streaming connections (owner: Solutions Eng)
